title: 2 Corinthians 1: chapter overview
paragraphs: The apostle blesses God for comfort in, and deliverance out of troubles.
He professes his own and his fellow-labourers' integrity.
Gives reasons for his not coming to them.

outline.text: The apostle blesses God for comfort in, and deliverance out of troubles.

Gives reasons for his not coming to them.

context: The second epistle to the Corinthians probably was written about a year after the first.
attribution: Matthew Henry, Concise Commentary (public domain). Historical Protestant interpretation; other traditions may read these passages differently.

title: 2 Corinthians 2: chapter overview
paragraphs: Reasons for the apostle not coming to Corinth.
Directions about restoring the repentant offender.
An account of his labours and success in spreading the gospel of Christ.

Their sufferings for the gospel were great, yet with rich supports.
Prospects of eternal glory keep believers from fainting under troubles.

The necessity of regeneration, and of reconciliation with God through Christ.

By affection for them, And by earnest concern, that they might have no fellowship with unbelievers and idolaters.

And in the comfort they and Titus had together.

He recommends Titus to them.

Explains what he was going to add in defence of his own character.
He gives an account of his labours, cares, sufferings, dangers, and deliverances.
